faq: Where does the extra information come from?
From your own data, public pages you point us to and sources whose terms allow this use. We do not scrape private data or buy contact lists. Each value shows its source.
Can you find personal emails or phone numbers for me?
No. We fill in business and product details only. We will not build lists of private individuals or break a website's rules to gather information.
How accurate will the filled data be?
It depends on the quality of your starting list. We test a sample with you, mark anything uncertain for review and report the match rate honestly rather than promise a number.
What file formats can you work with?
Google Sheets, Excel and CSV files, plus Airtable and most CRM exports. We return the result in the same format so you can load it straight back.

desc:
AI data enrichment for contacts and products fills the blank cells in lists you already own. Ecom Swift LLC sets up the work in your own files, adds details from sources you approve and marks every doubtful match for a person to check.

## What is data enrichment?

Data enrichment means adding missing details to records you already have. A product list might lack a category or material. A customer list might lack a country or company type. Enrichment matches each row against approved sources, including your other files, and writes the answer into the empty cell along with where it came from.

The result is a list that works properly in filters, reports, imports and email tools, instead of one that looks full but has holes where it counts.

## What goes wrong with half-empty lists

Gaps spread. A store import fails because a field is blank. A sales rep cannot filter by region, so they skip half the list. A report counts the same supplier three times because it is spelled three ways. Each gap is small, but the work around it adds up, and people stop trusting the sheet.

Guessing makes it worse. A tool that invents a value to fill a cell creates errors that look correct, and those are the hardest to find later. That is why this workflow records the source for each value and leaves unclear rows open.

## How enriched data improves your results

Complete records let you segment customers, sort products into the right collections and route orders without manual lookups. Marketing can send the right message to the right group. Operations can see which suppliers cover which products. Imports into a store, CRM or accounting tool run cleanly because required fields are present and formats are consistent.

The time saved is the main gain. A person who once searched the web for a few hundred rows now reviews only the rows the workflow marked as doubtful.

## What good enrichment includes

- A copy of your original file kept untouched, so nothing is lost.
- Clear rules for which columns may be filled and from which sources.
- A source note beside every filled value.
- Doubtful matches marked for review rather than guessed.
- Duplicate detection across rows that differ only in spelling or spacing.
- Standard formats for names, phone numbers, dates and country names.
- A before and after view, so you can compare the changes.
- A confidence marker for each value on larger setups.
- A repeatable run that handles new rows as they arrive.

## How we work

First we study a sample of your list and agree which gaps matter. We define the allowed sources with you, which can be your own supplier sheets, store exports, public company pages or other lists you supply. Then we build the matching steps in a spreadsheet tool or automation platform you own and run them on a test batch.

You review the test results, and we adjust the rules. The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in list size, number of columns, duplicate handling and whether the flow keeps running on new rows. We finish with handover notes explaining how to rerun it.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Back up the original file before any run.
- Tell us which columns are essential and which are nice to have.
- Check the flagged rows yourself, since you know your market.
- Keep a clear list of approved sources.
- Rerun on a small batch whenever the format of your file changes.

**Avoid:**
- Asking for details a source cannot reliably provide.
- Filling every cell at any cost, since an empty cell is better than a wrong one.
- Mixing several unrelated lists in one sheet.
- Skipping the review of flagged rows.
- Collecting personal details of people who have not agreed to share them.

## Who it is for

A store owner with a supplier catalog missing sizes and categories can use it before a product import. A small business with an old customer list can clean it before an email campaign. An operations lead merging two spreadsheets after a team change can use it to catch duplicates and unify formats.

## What we need from you

Send the file or share it with us as an editor, plus a short note on the columns to fill and the sources you trust. Please remove any data you are not allowed to share. We never ask for passwords, and any tool access is given through a limited member or collaborator account that you control.
